video.title: You’re Not Ready for What’s Coming: Robert Scoble on AI + Future Tech

summary: Koerner Office host Chris Koerner interviews futurist Robert Scoble about AI, wearables (smart glasses, Vision Pro), autonomous cars (Waymo vs Tesla), Neuralink, humanoid robots and the US-China race. Scoble argues AI is still underhyped, that people resist new technology until they try it, and that this boom is far bigger than the dot-com era. Almost no concrete business ideas or numbers are given; the only practical advice is to ask AI to do market research and to find niches the big labs will not serve. The video is mostly trend commentary and speculation.

warnings.warning: Brain-computer interfaces that write to the brain raise free-will and manipulation concerns.

quote.text: when you have wires on your brain, you have no free will anymore really.
quote.speaker: Robert Scoble

warnings.warning: AGI-era systems with autonomy and control of infrastructure such as the power grid could cause serious harm.

quote.text: We're going to turn our electrical grid into AI run, right? Well, if the AI decides you don't need electricity today, what does that do?
quote.speaker: Robert Scoble

warnings.warning: Customer research can mislead on future products because customers cannot imagine what does not exist yet.

quote.text: People can't they don't think about the future because that's not their deal.
quote.speaker: Robert Scoble

lessons.lesson: New technology is resisted at first by most people, so early adoption of disruptive tools is where advantage lies.

quote.text: I noticed this early in my career that people resist change. They don't like new ideas.
quote.speaker: Robert Scoble

lessons.lesson: Customers often reject what they have not experienced; watch behaviour after exposure (e.g. Google staff all looking at phones within three rides) rather than stated preferences.

quote.text: They all broke the rule in three rides.
quote.speaker: Robert Scoble

lessons.lesson: Data and user scale create flywheels in AI: more users make the system smarter, favouring incumbents, so small players should avoid head-on competition.

quote.text: The users make the system smarter. The more users you have, the smarter the system gets.
quote.speaker: Robert Scoble

lessons.lesson: Constraints drive creativity and entrepreneurship, as in Israel's startup density.

quote.text: the only thing we got is our brains.
quote.speaker: Robert Scoble

lessons.lesson: Use AI itself as a research assistant and idea validator before building.
Early adoption of new hardware often comes through enterprise use cases before consumers.
The AI boom is larger and faster than the dot-com era, with funding at a far higher scale, so timing and speed matter.

quote.text: No comparison. This is way bigger.
quote.speaker: Robert Scoble

evidence_quality.rationale: Trend commentary and speculation from a futurist with no first-hand business and almost no numbers or concrete business ideas; the host admits the ideas question was answered only generically.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Host promotes TK Owners ($99/month community) and his newsletter/podcast; Scoble promotes his X account and lists.
